Difference and system GMM for dynamic panels

Source: R/dpnl.R
gmmpnl.Rd

The generalized method of moments estimators of a dynamic panel with unit effects: the difference estimator of Arellano and Bond (1991) and the system estimator of Arellano and Bover (1995) and Blundell and Bond (1998), with the instrument matrix built as Roodman (2009) describes it. Andreatta et al. (2023, pp. 1372-1374, table 3) fit the logged rate of waste crime in Italian provinces this way: one-step system GMM with robust errors, time effects, the lagged rate and four enforcement and organised-crime variables instrumented GMM-style by their second and third lags, the AR(1) and AR(2) tests, the Hansen test, the Hansen test of the differenced equations alone and the difference-in-Hansen test of the level instruments, with no more instruments than provinces.

Usage

gmmpnl(
  y,
  x = NULL,
  unit,
  time,
  ylag = 1,
  gmm = NULL,
  iv = NULL,
  z = NULL,
  lagmin = 2,
  lagmax = Inf,
  collapse = FALSE,
  type = "system",
  trans = "fd",
  steps = 1,
  robust = TRUE,
  wc = NULL,
  small = FALSE,
  hmat = "ab",
  cons = TRUE,
  tdum = TRUE,
  ar = 2,
  level = 0.95
)

# S3 method for class 'gmmpnl'
plot(x, ..., main = NULL, col = NULL, pal = NULL)

Arguments

y

The outcome of each row: finite numbers.

x

NULL or the regressors: a numeric matrix or data frame, one row per row of y; the column names name them. For plot(), a gmmpnl result.

unit

The unit of each row: labels.

time

The period of each row: numbers; each unit at most once per period.

ylag

The lags of y among the regressors: a whole number from 0 (default 1, the first-order model of Arellano and Bond 1991, eq 1).

gmm

NULL or the names of columns of x instrumented GMM-style, as the lagged outcome is.

iv

NULL (every column of x not in gmm) or the names of the columns of x that instrument themselves, IV-style; character(0) for none.

z

NULL or excluded IV-style instruments: a numeric matrix or data frame, one row per row of y.

lagmin, lagmax

The lags of the GMM-style instruments: one value, or one per GMM-style variable (the lagged outcome first); whole numbers from 1, lagmax also Inf. The defaults 2 and Inf take every lag valid for an endogenous variable (Arellano and Bond 1991, sec. 2; Roodman 2009, sec. 3.2).

collapse

TRUE for one instrument per lag rather than per lag and period (Roodman 2009, sec. 3.2); default FALSE, the full set of Arellano and Bond.

type

"system" (default, Blundell and Bond 1998; the default of Roodman's xtabond2) or "diff" (Arellano and Bond 1991).

trans

"fd" (first differences, default, Arellano and Bond 1991) or "fod" (forward orthogonal deviations, Arellano and Bover 1995).

steps

1 (default; Andreatta et al. 2023 and the default of xtabond2) or 2 (the two-step estimator).

robust

TRUE (default) for the robust one-step variance and Windmeijer's correction of the two-step variance; FALSE for the conventional one-step variance and the uncorrected two-step variance.

wc

NULL (default: as robust) or TRUE or FALSE for Windmeijer's (2005) correction of the two-step variance; it must agree with robust.

small

FALSE (default) or TRUE for the small-sample variance, t statistics and an F test, as above.

hmat

"ab" (default), "dpd" or "id": H of the one-step weight, as above (Roodman 2009, secs. 3.3-3.4).

cons

TRUE (default) for a constant in the level equation of system GMM; ignored by difference GMM, which removes it.

tdum

TRUE (default) for time dummies, which Roodman (2009, sec. 3.3) advises so that the errors are not correlated across units.

ar

The highest order of the Arellano-Bond tests: a whole number from 0 (default 2, as xtabond2).

level

The confidence level of the intervals.

...

Passed to the base-graphics call.

main

NULL (a default title) or one string.

col

NULL (the palette) or colours.

pal

NULL (the session palette, see plotopt()) or a palette name for blpal().

Value

An object of class gmmpnl, a list: coef (term, est, se, z (t with small), p, lo, hi); tests (test, stat, df, p: AR(1) to AR(ar), Sargan, Hansen and, for system GMM, the Hansen test without the level GMM-style instruments and the difference-in-Hansen test, or their Sargan counterparts with the conventional one-step variance); wald, one row (test, "Wald" or "F", stat, df1, df2, p); fit, one row: n (the rows of the transformed equation for difference GMM, of the levels for system GMM, as xtabond2 counts), groups, inst, omin, oavg, omax (rows per group), steps, k and sigma2; vcov; inst, the instruments' names; dropped, the time dummies dropped; dummies, those kept; note; type; trans; robust; small; and level.

Details

The model is `y_it = a_1 y_i,t-1 + ... + a_L y_i,t-L + x_it b + d_t + u_i

  • v_itwithL = ylag. Periods are the distinct values of timein order: lags count positions in that order, and a unit without a row in a period has a gap there. A row enters the levels when the unit has theylag periods before it; the transformed equation is the first difference of two such rows in consecutive periods (trans = "fd"), or the forward orthogonal deviation of a row from the mean of the unit's later rows, scaled by sqrt(T / (T + 1)) and dated one period later (trans = "fod"`, Arellano and Bover 1995, sec. 3; Roodman 2009, eq 21), which loses no more than the last row of a unit with gaps.

GMM-style instruments (Roodman 2009, sec. 3.2) are made for the lagged outcome (when ylag > 0, first) and for the columns of x named in gmm: for the transformed equation dated t, the levels of the variable at t - l for l from lagmin to lagmax, zero where the unit has no row, one column per period and lag, or one per lag with collapse = TRUE. For the level equation of system GMM, the difference at t - lagmin + 1 (one column per period, or one); the other lags are redundant (Roodman 2009, sec. 3.4). Lags count from the variable: the default lagmin = 2 takes y_i,t-2 and earlier for the equation in t, the standard choice for an endogenous variable, and lagmin = 1 treats a column as predetermined. IV-style instruments (one column each, transformed in the transformed equation and in levels in the level equation, Roodman 2009, eq 24) are the columns of x in iv, the columns of z, the time dummies and, in system GMM, the constant (which is in the level equation only). Columns of instruments that are zero throughout are dropped; time dummies collinear with the other regressors in the stacked equations are dropped, and named in dropped.

The one-step weight is (sum_i Z_i' H_i Z_i)^-1. With hmat = "ab" (the default), H_i is what the errors' variance would be with independent, homoskedastic idiosyncratic errors and no unit effects in the level equation: M M' for the transformed rows (2 on the diagonal and -1 next to it for differences, the identity for deviations), M between transformed and level rows and the identity for the levels (Roodman 2009, eqs 22-23 and 26); "dpd" zeroes the blocks between the equations, and "id" takes the identity throughout, as Blundell and Bond (1998) did. The two-step weight is the inverse of sum_i Z_i' e_i e_i' Z_i with the one-step residuals. A singular weight matrix is replaced by its Moore-Penrose inverse, and the result says so. With robust = TRUE (the default) the one-step variance is the robust sandwich (Roodman 2009, eq 15) and the two-step variance is corrected as Windmeijer (2005) shows (Roodman 2009, eq 18); with robust = FALSE the one-step variance is the conventional s2 (X'Z A Z'X)^-1, eq 14 with Var(z e) = s2 Z'HZ, A = (Z'HZ)^-1 and s2 as for Sargan's statistic below, and the two-step variance is the uncorrected (X'Z A_2 Z'X)^-1 (Roodman 2009, p. 96). wc is the older name of the two-step choice: left NULL it follows robust, and a value that contradicts robust, or wc with one step, is refused. With small = TRUE the variance is multiplied by n / (n - k) (n the rows reported in fit, k the coefficients), and the coefficients have t statistics and the joint test is an F test, both on the groups less one (less nothing without a constant) degrees of freedom. Roodman (2009, p. 123) describes the option of xtabond2 only as "small-sample corrections to the covariance matrix estimate, resulting in t-test instead of z-test statistics for the coefficients and an F test instead of a Wald chi2 test for overall fit"; the degrees of freedom are those of his outputs (F(16, 140) for 140 groups without a constant, p. 113; F(12, 139) with one, p. 118), and the factor n / (n - k) is this function's reading, as the paper gives none.

The Arellano-Bond statistics (Arellano and Bond 1991, eqs 8-9) are those of serial correlation of orders 1 to ar in the differenced residuals of the estimate reported, also after deviations, with the variance's terms taken from that estimate's residuals, weight and variance (Roodman 2009, sec. 3.5), and with the error variance taken as s2 H for the conventional one-step variance (Roodman 2009, n. 19, the covariances of independent homoskedastic errors through the transformation and the differences, whatever hmat); AR(2) is the one that tests the instruments. Hansen's statistic is that of the two-step estimate, whichever step is reported, as robust overidentification tests need (Roodman 2009, sec. 2.5); Sargan's is that of the one-step residuals, e'Z (Z'HZ)^-1 Z'e / s2 with s2 the sum of the squared one-step residuals of the transformed equation over the sum of their diagonal elements of H (this function's estimate of the variance; Arellano and Bond 1991, p. 282, write the statistic with an estimate of it). In system GMM the Hansen test without the GMM-style instruments of the level equation re-estimates the model with the rest, weighted by the corresponding block of the full two-step moment variance (Roodman 2009, n. 24), and the difference-in-Hansen statistic is the full statistic less that one, on as many degrees of freedom as there are instruments left out. With the conventional one-step variance Sargan's statistic is the one reported for the instruments, and the difference test is the difference-in-Sargan, the model re-estimated with the block of Z'HZ (Roodman 2009, n. 24). wald is the joint test of the coefficients other than the constant. Every test is on m - k degrees of freedom or fewer, m the instruments and k the coefficients. When the instruments outnumber the groups, note says so (Roodman 2009, sec. 2.6). Inference is normal unless small = TRUE. Andreatta et al. describe their instruments both as "their second and third lags" (p. 1373) and as "Lag 2 and earlier lags" (table 3, note); lagmin and lagmax take either reading.

The plot draws the coefficients other than the constant and the time dummies, with their intervals, and returns what it drew.

References

Arellano, M. and Bond, S. (1991). Some tests of specification for panel data: Monte Carlo evidence and an application to employment equations. The Review of Economic Studies, 58(2), 277-297. doi:10.2307/2297968

Arellano, M. and Bover, O. (1995). Another look at the instrumental variable estimation of error-components models. Journal of Econometrics, 68(1), 29-51. doi:10.1016/0304-4076(94)01642-D

Blundell, R. and Bond, S. (1998). Initial conditions and moment restrictions in dynamic panel data models. Journal of Econometrics, 87(1), 115-143. doi:10.1016/S0304-4076(98)00009-8

Windmeijer, F. (2005). A finite sample correction for the variance of linear efficient two-step GMM estimators. Journal of Econometrics, 126(1), 25-51. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2004.02.005

Roodman, D. (2009). How to do xtabond2: an introduction to difference and system GMM in Stata. The Stata Journal, 9(1), 86-136. doi:10.1177/1536867X0900900106

Andreatta, D., Favarin, S., Lisciandra, M. and Millemaci, E. (2023). Digging into waste: an analysis of waste crime in the Italian provinces. Regional Studies, 57(7), 1367-1379. doi:10.1080/00343404.2022.2135697

Examples

# 60 provinces over 8 years: a logged rate with persistence 0.5 and one
# endogenous driver, simulated
set.seed(7)
d <- expand.grid(year = 2010:2017, prov = paste0("p", 1:60))
u <- rnorm(60)[as.integer(substring(d$prov, 2))]
d$enf <- u + rnorm(480)
d$y <- 0
for (i in which(d$year > 2010)) {
  d$y[i] <- 0.5 * d$y[i - 1] + 0.3 * d$enf[i] + u[i] + rnorm(1)
}
r <- gmmpnl(d$y, d["enf"], d$prov, d$year, gmm = "enf", lagmax = 3,
            collapse = TRUE)
r
#> gmmpnl: system GMM (fd), step 1, 420 rows, 60 groups, 13 instruments
